title: Directories & registries
description: Where to discover more: MCP registries, awesome-lists, skill and plugin marketplaces.

items.name: ComposioHQ/awesome-claude-skills
items.description: Curated list of 1,000+ Claude skills and plugins across Claude.ai, Claude Code and other agents.
items.why: Good discovery source; vet individual skills before installing.

items.name: awesome-claude-code
items.description: Hand-picked collection of resources for Claude Code: skills, hooks, slash commands, plugins.
items.verdictNote: adopt: main discovery list for Claude Code skills, hooks and tools
items.why: About 280 curated entries, updated 2026-10-24. Submissions go through a form checked by a bot, not a quality review, so vet each tool. Licence is NonCommercial-NoDerivatives: link to it, don't copy its contents into another published list.

items.name: BehiSecc/awesome-claude-skills
items.description: Awesome-list of Claude skills (about 8.4k stars as of April 2026 per Star History).
items.why: Alternative skills list; smaller than Composio.

items.name: claudemarketplaces.com
items.description: Independent directory of Claude Code plugins, skills and MCP servers ranked by installs, stars and votes.
items.why: Handy browsing; not affiliated with Anthropic.

items.name: MCP Registry
items.description: Community-driven registry service for MCP servers; live at registry.modelcontextprotocol.io.
items.why: Canonical discovery source for MCP servers.

items.name: punkpeye/awesome-mcp-servers
items.description: Large categorized list of MCP servers, linked to glama.ai/mcp/servers.
items.why: Largest MCP index; use to find YouTube/video/image/social servers.

items.name: Glama MCP multimedia category
items.description: Glama directory category for multimedia MCP servers.
items.why: Browse for vetted media servers.

items.name: Glama MCP servers directory
items.description: MCP server directory backing awesome-mcp-servers.
items.why: Search for YouTube/social MCPs.

items.name: awesome-motion-design-agent-skills
items.description: A map of 5 first-party skills, 10 engine projects (GSAP, Motion, R3F, Remotion, Anime.js, Rive, dotLottie, Phaser) and 7 third-party packs, with link checks and advice to scan third-party packs before installing. Search also showed a larger catalogue, zhuyansen/awesome-claude-video-skills (about 180 repos, each security-graded): not opened.
items.verdictNote: REFERENCE: use as a directory; never install from a list without reading the skill.
items.why: 2 stars; counts are 'discovery signals, not rankings'
items.source: research 2026-10: content, motion, 3D and game tools

items.name: awesome-selfhosted
items.description: The main directory of free software you can run on your own server (about 1,400 linked projects): automation, analytics, media, CRM, docs, mail, monitoring and more, each with licence and language. Last commit 2026-10-22.
items.verdictNote: adopt: first stop before paying for a SaaS tool
items.why: Best source of self-hostable alternatives (n8n, Postiz-style schedulers, analytics) to keep monthly costs down. Being listed is not a review: check each project's activity, licence and security before running it on a server.

items.name: awesome-python
items.description: Curated list of Python frameworks, libraries and tools by category (about 560 links): web, data, scraping, CLI, testing, ML and more. Last commit 2026-10-23.
items.verdictNote: adopt: reference when Claude writes Python
items.why: Useful for picking a well-known library instead of an obscure one when automation scripts are built in Python. A directory, not a quality ranking.

items.name: The Book of Secret Knowledge
items.description: Large collection of command-line tools, one-liners, cheat sheets, blogs and security resources for sysadmins and DevOps.
items.why: Handy for server and network troubleshooting, but last commit 2024-11-19, so some links and tools are stale. Includes offensive-security tools: use those only on systems you own or are authorised to test.

items.name: awesome-go
items.description: Curated list of Go frameworks, libraries and software (about 3,000 links), with quality requirements for new entries. Last commit 2026-10-23.
items.verdictNote: reference: only if a project is written in Go
items.why: Well maintained, but current projects use Node.js and Python; useful mainly when choosing Go-based self-hosted tools.

items.name: awesome-nodejs
items.description: Curated Node.js packages and resources by category (CLI, HTTP, databases, testing, scraping and more) from Sindre Sorhus. Last commit 2026-09-02.
items.verdictNote: adopt: reference when Claude writes Node.js
items.why: Node.js runs the MCP servers and most scripts, and this list is strictly curated, so it's a good place to pick dependable packages.

items.name: awesome-cpp
items.description: Large curated list of C/C++ frameworks, libraries and resources (about 1,400 links), including embedded, audio, graphics, networking and game sections. Last commit 2026-10-10.
items.verdictNote: reference: for firmware and embedded projects
items.why: Useful when microcontroller or device firmware (ESP32/Arduino) needs a C++ library; not needed for web or Python work.

items.name: awesome-react
items.description: Curated React ecosystem list: tutorials, state management, routing, UI, testing, frameworks. Last commit 2026-09-04.
items.why: Good map of the React ecosystem when a website or React Three Fiber game is built; the licence is inconsistent, so link to it rather than copy.
items.license: unclear (badge says CC0, links CC BY 4.0; no LICENSE file)

items.name: awesome-react-components
items.description: About 560 React components and libraries by type: tables, forms, charts, maps, drag-and-drop, editors, UI kits. Last commit 2026-01-26.
items.verdictNote: reference: when a React site needs a specific component
items.why: Fastest way to find a ready-made component (charts, tables, editors). Check each component's own maintenance status; updates to the list slowed in 2026.

items.name: Awesome Hacking (Hack-with-Github)
items.description: A list of about 80 other security and hacking lists (pentesting, CTF, malware analysis, reverse engineering, web security). Last commit 2026-07-26.
items.verdictNote: reference: security learning and authorised testing only
items.why: Good entry point for security learning. Use offensive tools only on systems you own or have written permission to test (see the reverse-engineering compliance rule).

items.name: Papers We Love
items.description: Community collection of influential computer-science papers by topic (about 200 PDFs plus links), from distributed systems to AI. Last commit 2026-09-29.
items.why: Learning resource, not a tool. No repo licence; each paper keeps its own copyright.

items.name: awesome-design-patterns
items.description: Software and architecture design patterns by language and domain (cloud, microservices, serverless, ML, games). Last commit 2024-10-25.
items.why: Useful background for planning larger builds, but not updated for two years, so some links are stale.

items.name: GameDev-Resources (Kavex)
items.description: English list of about 320 game-dev links: 2D/3D/audio assets, engines and frameworks, ads and monetization, tools, tutorials. Each link is tagged paid, limited free, 100% free or open source. Last commit 2026-04-10.
items.verdictNote: reference: browse for discovery; check every licence yourself
items.why: The paid/free tags save time, but no licence file and no updates since April, so some links will be stale. The library's own asset-source entries already carry checked licences.

items.name: AI Game DevTools (AI-GDT)
items.description: Directory of 200+ AI tools for game development: LLMs, world models, agents, code, image, texture, shader, 3D model, animation, video, audio, music and singing voice, with a companion website. Last commit 2026-07-21.
items.verdictNote: reference: discovery list for AI game tools
items.why: Good map of research-grade AI tools by category, but mostly papers and repos with no quality or licence review, many needing big GPUs. Not updated since July.

items.name: GameDev (crazyshader)
items.description: Single Chinese-language README of game-dev links, heavy on Unity open-source projects, rendering and other awesome lists. No licence file. Last commit 2026-05-25.
items.why: Mostly links to other lists, in Chinese, with no descriptions or licence notes. Kavex/GameDev-Resources covers the English side better.

items.name: GameDevMind
items.description: Chinese-language knowledge map for game programmers and tech leads: fundamentals, game production, scaling, team management and live operations, with mind maps, runnable code, real incident cases and AI-collaboration notes. About 640 files; very active (2026-10-17).
items.verdictNote: reference: use with a translator for game-studio management and live-ops topics
items.why: Unusually deep on running a studio and live operations, not just code. Written in Chinese, so read it through translation or ask Claude to summarise a topic.
